posts.text: Two teams at Western Developers Society's Xcelerate built almost the exact same app without ever talking to each other. Turns out a lot of us are frustrated by figuring out what clubs at Western are actually up to. It can easily turn into mindless scrolling on Instagram. And more importantly, you can't follow a club you don't even know exists. So we built Keep Up, a unified events board for clubs across campus. Public speaking dropout turned public speaker?! A year ago I dropped out of my public speaking class, so giving a talk at the WITS+ lightning talks was a full circle moment for me. Back then I was scared. I talked quietly, rushed my points, and I was afraid of taking up space because I didn't feel important enough. “Why post about a competition you didn’t win?” I’ve heard that question a few times since my case competition last weekend. My answer is that I came home with new perspectives and a crash course in a field I’d never worked in before, and that feels worth sharing. Here’s my TLDR after talking with other participants and the winning teams: - Iterate fast. Proud to say I took home a win at my first-ever hackathon 🥇 ...in the spicy ramen eating competition. Hack the Hill III was my first-ever hackathon and honestly as a 4th year CS student I felt a little behind my peers not having much experience in events like this.
